name: Question 2
problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}4xy,\, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X>\frac{1}{2},Y>\frac{1}{2}).$
worked_solution:
If $f(x,y)$ is a joint probability density function for the random variables $X$ and $Y$ and $A⊂{R}^{2},$ then

$$
P((X,Y)\in A)={∬}_{A}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

Notice that $f(x,y)$ is nonnegative in the region $D=[0,1]\times [0,1],$ and the event $A={X>0.5,Y>0.5}$ corresponds to a subset of $D,$ shown as the shaded region below:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14069972/assets/7e81ce16404bc6c5c826f79a88519bd6216156f5bb0f8af1eae41f19ca495de5.png)

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>\frac{1}{2},Y>\frac{1}{2}) & ={∬}_{A}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}{\int }_{1/2}^{1}4xy\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}[{\int }_{1/2}^{1}4xy\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}{[2{x}^{2}y]}_{x=1/2}^{x=1}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}\frac{3y}{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{3{y}^{2}}{4}]}_{1/2}^{1} \\  & =\frac{9}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$
